four steps before just inside arena
high speed before floor bounce sets up low grazing trajectory

counterfactual.change: Reduced body radius from 0.96005868990278675 to 0.5. Smaller radius needs less clearance and positional correction succeeds, so arena containment holds; test confirms large radius is key to failure.

explanation: After a high-speed fall and floor bounce (step 180 speed ~12.7), the body with large radius 0.96 retains vx~2.71 and bounces low near the floor (y~1.07-1.19). Substep count drops to 2 per step while traversing toward the right arena boundary. The arena boundary collision/positional correction fails to keep the centre at least -r+0.15 inside; overshoot grows from -0.0006 at step 190 to 0.088 at 192, 0.133 at 193, exceeding tolerance 0.15 at step 194 with 0.178. Likely cause is simultaneous floor contact and right-boundary contact with too few substeps/weak correction for large radius, letting x drift outside.
vision_note: From steps 191 to 194 the red ball near the floor drifts rightward and progressively crosses the thick black right boundary of the arena. By step 194 a large portion of the circle is visibly outside the arena.
